meta.provenance: Authored from model knowledge (cutoff Jan 2026). Original explanations — not copied from the Blender Manual. Shortcuts/menu paths are factual data. Run scripts/command-scrapers/scrape-blender.mjs to sync with the live manual (manual text is CC-BY-SA 4.0 — do not import its prose without attribution).
meta.iconNote: Blender's icon set ships under GPL with Blender; app renders software chip fallback.

commands.name: Absolute Grid Snap
commands.menu: 3D Viewport — Header — Snapping Dropdown — Absolute Grid Snap
commands.description: With grid snapping active, this option snaps to fixed grid positions rather than moving in grid-sized steps from the start point. Turn it on for CAD-like behaviour where everything lands exactly on the planning grid.

commands.name: Add Bézier Curve
commands.menu: 3D Viewport — Object Mode — Add — Curve — Bézier
commands.description: Creates a Bézier curve object, edited through control points and handles. Curves are ideal for road centrelines, handrail paths, swept profiles and any geometry defined by a line rather than a surface.

commands.name: Add Camera
commands.description: Adds a camera object to the scene. Keep several cameras for fixed viewpoints — key exterior views, interior vignettes — and switch the active one per shot.

commands.name: Add Empty
commands.description: Creates a non-rendering null object useful as a pivot, mirror centre, array offset target or group handle. Architects often use empties to drive Array and Mirror modifiers for repetitive structure.

commands.name: Add Grease Pencil Object
commands.menu: 3D Viewport — Object Mode — Add — Grease Pencil
commands.description: Creates a Grease Pencil object for drawing 2D strokes that live in 3D space. Architects use it to sketch design options over a model, red-line reviews, and add hand-drawn linework to renders.

commands.name: Add Light
commands.description: Adds a Point, Sun, Spot or Area light. Sun gives parallel daylight for exteriors; Area lights are the workhorses of interior renders, standing in for windows and fittings.

commands.name: Add Modifier
commands.description: Adds a non-destructive modifier to the active object from the generate, deform and physics categories. Modifiers stack top-to-bottom and can be reordered, disabled or applied — the heart of parametric-style modelling in Blender.

commands.name: Add Node
commands.description: Opens the add menu in any node editor — Shader, Geometry Nodes or Compositor — with a search field at the top. Type-search is usually faster than browsing the categories.

commands.name: Add Object
commands.description: Opens the Add menu to create meshes, curves, empties, lights, cameras and more at the 3D cursor. Move the cursor first with Shift+RMB to place new geometry exactly where you want it.

commands.name: Adjust Last Operation
commands.description: Reopens the floating panel of options for the operation you just ran, letting you tweak values such as bevel width or number of cuts after the fact. Note it disappears as soon as you do something else.

commands.name: Adjust Voxel Size
commands.description: Interactively sets the voxel size used by the next remesh, shown as a grid overlay. Smaller voxels keep more detail but cost polygons — tune it before each Voxel Remesh.

commands.name: Align Camera to View
commands.menu: 3D Viewport — View — Align View — Align Active Camera to View
commands.description: Snaps the active camera to match your current viewport view exactly. The natural workflow: navigate freely until the composition looks right, then commit it to the camera.

commands.name: Annotate Tool
commands.description: Draws lightweight annotation strokes available in almost every editor, without creating a Grease Pencil object. Use it for throwaway notes and mark-ups during design reviews; for anything you want to keep and style, use a Grease Pencil object instead.

commands.name: Apply Modifier
commands.menu: Properties — Modifier Properties — Modifier Dropdown — Apply
commands.description: Bakes a modifier's result into the mesh permanently and removes it from the stack. Do this only when you are sure — applied booleans and arrays can no longer be adjusted parametrically.

commands.name: Apply Transforms
commands.description: Bakes the object's location, rotation and/or scale into its mesh data, resetting the transform channels to neutral. Apply scale in particular before using bevels, booleans or exporting — unapplied scale is a classic cause of wonky modifier results.

commands.name: Archimesh
commands.description: A community add-on (installed from the Extensions platform in Blender 4.2+) that generates parametric rooms, doors, windows, stairs and cabinets. Useful for fast early-stage layouts, though most practices outgrow it for detailed work.

commands.name: Archipack
commands.description: A community add-on (via the Extensions platform in 4.2+) offering editable parametric walls, openings, roofs, stairs and 2D-to-3D workflows, closer to a lightweight BIM toolkit than Archimesh. Worth evaluating if you build many conventional buildings directly in Blender.

commands.name: Array Modifier
commands.description: Repeats the object along an offset, with constant, relative or object-driven spacing, and arrays can be chained for grids. The workhorse for columns, fence posts, balustrades, stair treads and facade modules.

commands.name: Assign Material
commands.description: Applies the selected material slot to the faces currently selected in Edit Mode. Select the faces of one finish, pick the slot, press Assign — repeat per material.

commands.name: Auto Keying
commands.description: The record button in the Timeline: while enabled, any transform you make is keyframed automatically at the current frame. Powerful for blocking out camera moves, and dangerous if left on — stray edits become animation.

commands.name: Auto Merge Vertices
commands.menu: 3D Viewport — Edit Mode — Header — Options — Auto Merge
commands.description: When enabled, vertices moved onto other vertices weld automatically. With snapping active it gives a CAD-like drafting feel — drag a point onto a corner and the mesh joins itself.

commands.name: Average Islands Scale
commands.menu: UV Editor — UV — Average Islands Scale
commands.description: Rescales UV islands so texture density is consistent across the whole model. Without it, one brick texture can appear at different scales on different walls — instantly noticeable on architecture.

commands.name: Axis Constraint
commands.description: During a move, rotate or scale, pressing X, Y or Z locks the transform to that global axis; pressing the same key twice switches to the object's local axis. The foundation of accurate, orthogonal modelling.

commands.name: Batch Rename
commands.description: Renames many objects at once with find-and-replace, prefixes, suffixes or numbering. Invaluable for cleaning up imported CAD or IFC data with hundreds of generically named parts.

commands.name: Bevel
commands.menu: 3D Viewport — Edit Mode — Edge — Bevel Edges
commands.description: Rounds or chamfers the selected edges; scroll during the operation to add segments for a smoother profile. Nothing in the real world has a perfectly sharp arris — a small bevel catches highlights and makes renders read as built rather than digital.

commands.name: Bevel Modifier
commands.description: Applies a non-destructive bevel to the whole object, filtered by angle or edge weight. Set a small width and an angle limit and every hard arris in the model picks up a realistic softened edge for rendering.

commands.name: Bisect
commands.description: Slices the selected geometry along a plane you drag across the view, with options to clear either side and fill the cut. Perfect for section-style cuts through a model or trimming a massing block to a boundary.

commands.name: Bool Tool
commands.description: An add-on (bundled historically, via Extensions in 4.2+) that wraps Boolean modifiers in fast one-key operations — select cutter and target, apply difference, union or slice instantly. Speeds up opening-heavy facade work considerably.

commands.name: Boolean Modifier
commands.description: Cuts, intersects or unions the mesh with another object non-destructively. The standard way to punch window and door openings through walls — keep the cutter object live and openings stay adjustable.

commands.name: Box Mask
commands.menu: 3D Viewport — Sculpt Mode — Toolbar — Box Mask
commands.description: Drags a rectangle to mask part of the sculpt so brushes no longer affect it. Mask what you want to protect, then work freely on the rest.

commands.name: Box Select
commands.description: Drag a rectangle to select everything inside it; hold Ctrl while dragging to deselect instead. In Edit Mode, enable X-Ray first if you also want the geometry hidden behind front faces.

commands.name: Bridge Edge Loops
commands.menu: 3D Viewport — Edit Mode — Edge — Bridge Edge Loops
commands.description: Connects two selected edge loops with a band of faces, with options for cuts and smoothing along the way. Ideal for joining floor plates, connecting duct sections or lofting between two profiles.

commands.name: Center Cursor and Frame All
commands.description: Resets the 3D cursor to the world origin and zooms out to frame the whole scene in one stroke. A handy reset when both your cursor and your view have wandered.

commands.name: Checker Deselect
commands.menu: 3D Viewport — Edit Mode — Select — Checker Deselect
commands.description: Deselects every other element in the selection, leaving an alternating pattern. Combined with a face selection on a grid facade it builds instant chequerboard panel patterns.

commands.name: Choose Render Engine
commands.description: Switches between EEVEE (real-time, fast, approximate) and Cycles (path-traced, physically accurate, slower). A common architectural workflow is EEVEE for design iteration and Cycles for final images where accurate bounced light matters.

commands.name: Circle Select
commands.description: Paints a selection with a circular brush; scroll to resize the brush and press Escape or right-click to finish. Good for grabbing organic clusters of vertices.

commands.name: Clear Keyframes
commands.description: Deletes the keyframes on the current frame for the selected objects. Use the Dope Sheet instead when you need to prune keys across many frames at once.

commands.name: Clear Location
commands.menu: 3D Viewport — Object Mode — Object — Clear — Location
commands.description: Resets the object's location to the world origin. Useful for returning a reference block or asset to 0,0,0 before linking or exporting.

commands.name: Clear Mask
commands.menu: 3D Viewport — Sculpt Mode — Mask — Clear Mask
commands.description: Removes all masking so every part of the surface responds to brushes again. Do this whenever a brush mysteriously stops working — a forgotten mask is usually the culprit.

commands.name: Clear Parent
commands.menu: 3D Viewport — Object Mode — Object — Parent — Clear Parent
commands.description: Removes the parent relationship. Choose Clear and Keep Transformation to release the child without it jumping back to its pre-parented position.

commands.name: Clear Render Region
commands.menu: 3D Viewport — View — View Regions — Clear Render Region
commands.description: Removes the render region so full-frame rendering resumes. If renders are mysteriously cropped, a forgotten render region is almost always why.

commands.name: Clear Rotation
commands.menu: 3D Viewport — Object Mode — Object — Clear — Rotation
commands.description: Zeros the object's rotation, squaring it back up to the world axes. A fast fix for an asset imported or nudged off-axis.

commands.name: Clear Scale
commands.menu: 3D Viewport — Object Mode — Object — Clear — Scale
commands.description: Resets scale back to 1.0 on all axes, undoing any object-level scaling. Note this changes the object's size — to keep the size but normalise the values, use Apply Transforms instead.

commands.name: Clear Seam
commands.menu: 3D Viewport — Edit Mode — Edge — Clear Seam
commands.description: Removes the seam flag from the selected edges. Use it while iterating on an unwrap layout that is not falling flat cleanly.

commands.name: Clear Tilt
commands.menu: 3D Viewport — Edit Mode (Curve) — Control Points — Clear Tilt
commands.description: Resets any tilt on the selected control points to zero, untwisting the swept profile. The quick fix when a bevelled curve develops an unwanted corkscrew.

commands.name: Color Management
commands.description: Controls the view transform applied to renders — AgX (the default in 4.x) handles bright highlights gracefully, while Standard is flat and literal. Try AgX with a touch of extra contrast before reaching for heavy post-production.

commands.name: Convert Curve to Mesh
commands.menu: 3D Viewport — Object Mode — Object — Convert — Mesh
commands.description: Turns the curve, including any bevel or extrusion geometry, into an editable mesh. Do this when a swept element needs mesh-level detailing such as boolean cuts or bevelled ends.

commands.name: Convert to Mesh
commands.menu: 3D Viewport — Object Mode — Object — Convert — Mesh
commands.description: Converts curves, text or other object types into editable mesh geometry, baking any modifiers in the process. Do this when a swept profile or extruded text needs mesh-level editing — but keep a copy, as conversion is one-way.

commands.name: Copy Modifiers to Selected
commands.menu: 3D Viewport — Object — Link/Transfer Data — Copy Modifiers
commands.description: Copies the active object's whole modifier stack onto all other selected objects. Set up one wall's Solidify and Bevel once, then push the stack to every wall in the scene.

commands.name: Copy Objects
commands.menu: 3D Viewport — Object Mode — Object — Copy Objects
commands.description: Copies the selected objects to Blender's buffer, including between two open Blender windows or files. Pairs with Paste Objects to move assets across projects.

commands.name: Create New Collection
commands.menu: 3D Viewport — Object Mode — Object — Collection — Create New Collection
commands.description: Creates a fresh collection containing the selected objects. Combine with the Outliner to build a tidy, layer-like structure for large scenes.

commands.name: Curve Bevel Depth
commands.description: Gives the curve a round or custom profile swept along its length, turning a line into a tube or moulding. Set a profile object to sweep a skirting, cornice or handrail section along any path.

commands.name: Curve Modifier
commands.description: Bends the mesh along a curve object. Combined with an Array modifier it sweeps repeating elements — fencing, kerbs, cladding modules — along any curved path.

commands.name: Curve Tilt
commands.menu: 3D Viewport — Edit Mode (Curve) — Control Points — Tilt
commands.description: Rotates the curve's cross-section around its own axis at the selected control points. Use it to bank a swept handrail around a helical stair or correct a twisted extrusion.

commands.name: Cut Links
commands.description: Drag a line across node connections to sever them. The fastest way to disconnect several noodles at once while restructuring a material.

commands.name: Decimate Modifier
commands.description: Reduces polygon count while approximating the original shape, by collapsing, un-subdividing or planar merging. Use it to lighten heavy survey meshes and context models that are slowing the viewport.

commands.name: Delete
commands.description: Removes the selected objects from the scene after a confirmation. Pressing Delete does the same without asking.

commands.name: Delete (Edit Mode)
commands.description: Opens the delete menu for vertices, edges, faces, or subtler options such as Only Faces and Edge Loops. Choosing the right variant matters — deleting vertices takes connected faces with them, while Only Faces leaves the wireframe intact.

commands.name: Delete Hierarchy
commands.description: Deletes an object together with all of its children in one action from the Outliner. Safer than hunting down every child of a parented assembly manually.

commands.name: Depth of Field
commands.menu: Properties — Object Data (Camera) — Depth of Field
commands.description: Enables photographic focus blur on the camera, with a focus object or distance and an f-stop. A subtle wide-aperture blur pushes background context out of focus and draws the eye to the subject — use restraint for exterior shots.

commands.name: Deselect All
commands.description: Clears the current selection without touching anything else. Handy before starting a careful click-by-click selection.

commands.name: Displace Modifier
commands.description: Pushes vertices along their normals by the values of a texture. Drive it with a heightmap image to generate site terrain, or with noise for subtle surface irregularity on large planes.

commands.name: Dissolve Vertices
commands.menu: 3D Viewport — Edit Mode — Vertex — Dissolve Vertices
commands.description: Removes the selected vertices but heals the surrounding faces rather than leaving a hole. The difference from Delete is crucial: dissolve simplifies, delete destroys.

commands.name: Dope Sheet
commands.description: An editor showing every keyframe of every channel as blocks on a timeline, ideal for retiming — select keys and move or scale them like geometry. This is where you slide a whole camera move later or stretch it to last longer.

commands.name: Draw Brush
commands.description: The default sculpt brush, pulling the surface outward along the stroke (hold Ctrl to carve inward). Combined with a large radius and low strength it is a natural terrain-shaping tool.

commands.name: Draw Curve
commands.description: Freehand-draws a curve directly in the viewport, with automatic smoothing and optional projection onto surfaces. Useful for sketching paths over terrain or tracing a reference image.

commands.name: Duplicate Linked
commands.menu: 3D Viewport — Object Mode — Object — Duplicate Linked
commands.description: Duplicates the object but shares the same mesh data, so editing one instance updates all of them. Perfect for repeated components such as windows, chairs or balustrade panels — change the master and every copy follows.

commands.name: Duplicate Objects
commands.menu: 3D Viewport — Object Mode — Object — Duplicate Objects
commands.description: Copies the selection and drops you straight into a move; click to place or press Escape to leave the copy on top of the original. Each duplicate has independent mesh data, so edits will not propagate.

commands.name: Dynamic Topology
commands.description: Lets sculpt brushes add and remove geometry on the fly, so resolution follows your strokes instead of being fixed in advance. Powerful for freeform concept massing, but it destroys UVs and clean topology — keep it for study models.

commands.name: Edge Crease
commands.menu: 3D Viewport — Edit Mode — Edge — Edge Crease
commands.description: Sets a crease weight on selected edges so the Subdivision Surface modifier holds them sharper. Drag toward 1.0 for a hard corner, 0 for fully smooth — the way to keep crisp edges on subdivided furniture and joinery.

commands.name: Edge Length Overlay
commands.description: Displays the length of selected edges (plus optional angles and face areas) live in Edit Mode. Effectively turns Blender into a dimensioned modeller — every selected wall edge reports its true length as you work.

commands.name: Edge Loop Select
commands.menu: 3D Viewport — Edit Mode — Select — Select Loops — Edge Loops
commands.description: Selects an entire loop of connected edges in one click. On a clean quad mesh this instantly grabs a storey line, a mullion run or the full perimeter of an opening.

commands.name: Edge Ring Select
commands.menu: 3D Viewport — Edit Mode — Select — Select Loops — Edge Rings
commands.description: Selects the ring of parallel edges running perpendicular to the clicked edge. Combine with Loop Cut or Bevel to work across a whole band of geometry at once.

commands.name: Edge Select Mode
commands.description: Switches Edit Mode selection to edges — the natural mode for architectural work, where most operations run along wall lines, reveals and arrises.

commands.name: Edge Slide
commands.menu: 3D Viewport — Edit Mode — Edge — Edge Slide
commands.description: Pressing G twice slides the selected edge loop along the surface between its neighbours, preserving the surrounding shape. The safe way to reposition a loop without distorting curvature.

commands.name: Export FBX
commands.description: Exports to FBX for Unreal, Unity, Twinmotion and other real-time tools. Apply scale and check the axis settings — unapplied transforms are the top cause of models arriving at the wrong size in engines.

commands.name: Export glTF
commands.description: Exports to glTF/GLB with materials and textures packed into a single portable file. The format of choice for web viewers and AR presentations of a design.

commands.name: Export OBJ
commands.description: Exports selected or all geometry as OBJ, with options for materials, triangulation and axis conventions. A safe lowest-common-denominator format for sending models to renderers and CAD colleagues.

commands.name: Export STL
commands.description: Exports geometry as STL for 3D printing physical models. Check the mesh is watertight first — Voxel Remesh or the 3D Print Toolbox can close a leaky massing model before printing.

commands.name: Extrude Along Normals
commands.menu: 3D Viewport — Edit Mode — Mesh — Extrude — Extrude Faces Along Normals
commands.description: Extrudes multiple faces along their own normals in unison, keeping consistent offset even around corners. Ideal for thickening several walls of a shell outward at once.

commands.name: Extrude Curve
commands.description: Extends the curve from a selected end control point, adding a new segment that follows the mouse. The point-by-point way to build a precise path or profile.

commands.name: Extrude Individual Faces
commands.menu: 3D Viewport — Edit Mode — Mesh — Extrude — Extrude Individual Faces
commands.description: Extrudes each selected face separately along its own normal instead of moving them as one region. Use it to grow separate piers or fins from a set of faces in one action.

commands.name: Extrude Region
commands.description: Pulls new geometry out of the selected vertices, edges or faces, keeping them connected to the original mesh. The fundamental way to grow a plan outline into walls or push a footprint up into a massing model.

commands.name: Extrude to Cursor
commands.description: Extrudes the selection directly to the clicked position — click, click, click to trace out a connected run of edges. Quick for sketching wall centrelines or profile outlines vertex by vertex.

commands.name: Face Select Mode
commands.description: Switches Edit Mode selection to faces, ideal for extruding, insetting or assigning materials to whole surfaces.

commands.name: Fill
commands.description: Fills the selected boundary with triangles. Quick for capping irregular openings, though Grid Fill gives cleaner quad topology where the boundary allows it.

commands.name: Flip Normals
commands.menu: 3D Viewport — Edit Mode — Mesh — Normals — Flip
commands.description: Reverses the direction of the selected face normals. Use it surgically on individual faces the recalculate options cannot resolve, such as non-manifold surfaces.

commands.name: Frame All
commands.description: Fits every visible object into the viewport. A quick way to recover when you have zoomed off into empty space or lost the model.

commands.name: Frame Selected
commands.description: Zooms and centres the view on whatever is selected, and resets the orbit pivot to it. Reach for this whenever orbiting starts pivoting around the wrong part of the scene.

commands.name: Front View
commands.description: Snaps the viewport to look straight down the -Y axis, the equivalent of a front elevation. Pair it with orthographic projection for drawing-like views of a building.

commands.name: Geometry Nodes Modifier
commands.menu: Properties — Modifier Properties — Generate — Geometry Nodes
commands.description: Attaches a node graph that generates or processes geometry procedurally, edited in the Geometry Nodes workspace. For architects it unlocks parametric facades, scattering of planting, and rule-driven repetition that updates when inputs change.

commands.name: Grab Brush
commands.description: Grabs the surface under the brush and drags it wholesale, like pulling on fabric. The most direct brush for repositioning landforms and adjusting massing without changing detail.

commands.name: Graph Editor
commands.description: Shows animation as editable curves of value against time, with handles like a Bézier curve. The place to smooth a camera path's acceleration so a walkthrough glides instead of lurching.

commands.name: Grease Pencil Draw Mode
commands.description: The mode for sketching strokes onto a Grease Pencil object, with brushes, colours and placement options (on surfaces, on a plane, or in screen space). Drawing onto surfaces lets you annotate directly on a facade.

commands.name: Grease Pencil Draw Tool
commands.description: The freehand pen for Grease Pencil strokes, with pressure-sensitive radius and opacity on a tablet. Treat it like a fineliner over the model — quick option sketches without leaving the 3D scene.

commands.name: Grease Pencil Erase
commands.description: Erases Grease Pencil strokes, by point, stroke or soft dissolve. Hold Ctrl while using the Draw tool for quick temporary erasing.

commands.name: Grease Pencil Layers
commands.description: Grease Pencil objects hold strokes on stacked layers with independent opacity, blending and visibility. Keep sketch iterations on separate layers so design options can be toggled like tracing paper.

commands.name: Grease Pencil Line Tool
commands.description: Drags out straight Grease Pencil strokes, with siblings for arcs, curves, boxes and circles in the same toolbar group. The tool for tidy diagrammatic overlays rather than freehand sketching.

commands.name: Grid Fill
commands.menu: 3D Viewport — Edit Mode — Face — Grid Fill
commands.description: Fills a closed boundary loop with a clean grid of quads, blending to match the surrounding surface. The best way to cap cylinders and rebuild missing patches with usable topology.

commands.name: Hide Selected
commands.description: Temporarily hides the selected objects (or selected geometry in Edit Mode) from the viewport. Use it to get obstructions out of the way while you work inside a building.

commands.name: Hide Unselected
commands.description: Hides everything except the current selection — an instant isolate. Unlike Local View it persists until you unhide, which suits longer focused sessions.

commands.name: Image Texture Node
commands.menu: Shader Editor — Add — Texture — Image Texture
commands.description: Loads an image and outputs its colours for use in a material, mapped through the object's UVs. The basis of any photographic or scanned material — brick, timber, stone — applied to architecture.

commands.name: Import FBX
commands.description: Imports FBX files, the common interchange for game engines and 3ds Max/Maya assets, including hierarchies, materials and animation. Furniture manufacturers' asset downloads frequently arrive in FBX.

commands.name: Import glTF
commands.description: Imports glTF/GLB, the modern open standard for 3D assets on the web, with PBR materials that map cleanly onto Blender's Principled BSDF. Increasingly the best-behaved format for downloaded assets.

commands.name: Import Images as Planes
commands.menu: 3D Viewport — Object Mode — Add — Image — Mesh Plane
commands.description: Creates a correctly proportioned, textured plane from an image file in one step (built into the Add menu from Blender 4.2; previously the bundled Images as Planes add-on). Ideal for site photos, reference elevations and cut-out people or trees in visuals.

commands.name: Import OBJ
commands.description: Imports OBJ geometry with materials, a near-universal exchange format from SketchUp, Rhino and render asset libraries. Watch the scale and up-axis options — other packages often disagree with Blender's Z-up metres.

commands.name: Import STL
commands.description: Imports STL triangle meshes, the standard for 3D printing and much scan data. Expect dense triangulated geometry — Limited Dissolve and Decimate are your friends afterwards.

commands.name: Increment Snap
commands.description: Holding Ctrl during a transform snaps to the active snapping increment or target — grid steps by default, or vertices/faces if snapping is configured. It temporarily inverts the snap toggle, so it also disables snapping when snapping is already on.

commands.name: Insert Keyframe
commands.description: Records the current value of location, rotation, scale or other channels at the current frame. Two keyframes on a camera are enough for a simple architectural fly-through; hover over any property field and press I to key that property alone.

commands.name: Inset Faces
commands.menu: 3D Viewport — Edit Mode — Mesh — Inset Faces
commands.description: Creates a smaller face inside the selected one, connected by a border — press I again during the operation to inset each face individually. The classic first step for window and panel openings: inset, then extrude the inner face inward.

commands.name: Interactive Mirror
commands.description: Mirrors the selection interactively — press X, Y or Z after invoking to choose the axis, relative to the current pivot point. For live, editable symmetry prefer the Mirror Modifier.

commands.name: Invert Brush Stroke
commands.description: Holding Ctrl while sculpting reverses the brush direction — Draw carves in instead of building up. Valleys and cuttings are just inverted hills.

commands.name: Invert Mask
commands.menu: 3D Viewport — Sculpt Mode — Mask — Invert Mask
commands.description: Swaps masked and unmasked regions. A standard rhythm: mask an area, invert, and sculpt only inside it.

commands.name: Invert Selection
commands.description: Swaps selected and unselected. Often the fastest route: select the few things you do not want, then invert.

commands.name: Join
commands.description: Merges all selected objects into the active (last-selected) one, keeping material assignments. Use it to consolidate loose parts before export or when a wall built from pieces should behave as one object.

commands.name: Join in New Frame
commands.menu: Shader Editor — Node — Join in New Frame
commands.description: Wraps the selected nodes in a labelled frame that moves as one block. Frames plus labels are the difference between a readable material graph and spaghetti.

commands.name: Jump to End
commands.description: Moves the playhead to the final frame of the range — useful for checking the closing composition of a camera move.

commands.name: Jump to Next Keyframe
commands.description: Skips the playhead forward to the next keyframe of the selected object. Much faster than scrubbing when editing a sparse camera animation.

commands.name: Jump to Previous Keyframe
commands.description: Skips the playhead back to the previous keyframe of the selected object. The counterpart to Jump to Next Keyframe.

commands.name: Jump to Start
commands.description: Moves the playhead to the first frame of the range. Get in the habit before playing back a take from the top.

commands.name: Knife
commands.description: Cuts new edges freehand across faces by clicking points; press A to constrain to angles, Z to cut through the whole mesh, and Enter to confirm. Use it to carve arbitrary lines — a diagonal brace, a crack, a custom panel joint — where loop cuts cannot go.

commands.name: Knife Project
commands.menu: 3D Viewport — Edit Mode — Mesh — Knife Project
commands.description: Projects the outline of another object (often a curve or text) through the view onto the mesh being edited, cutting its shape in. A powerful way to cut signage, logos or complex opening shapes into a facade.

commands.name: Lasso Select
commands.description: Draw a freehand loop around the items you want selected. Useful when a rectangular box would catch too much.

commands.name: Lattice Modifier
commands.description: Deforms the mesh through a low-resolution lattice cage — move a handful of lattice points and the dense mesh follows smoothly. A controllable way to taper, twist or gently bend a whole massing model.

commands.name: Limited Dissolve
commands.menu: 3D Viewport — Edit Mode — Mesh — Delete — Limited Dissolve
commands.description: Dissolves edges and vertices that lie within an angle threshold of being flat, merging coplanar faces into larger n-gons. The single most useful cleanup for triangulated CAD and IFC imports — it turns tessellated walls back into simple faces.

commands.name: Link/Transfer Data
commands.menu: 3D Viewport — Object Mode — Object — Link/Transfer Data
commands.description: Copies data from the active object to the other selected ones: materials, modifiers, object data and more. A quick way to push one wall's material or modifier stack onto twenty others.

commands.name: Lock Camera to View
commands.menu: 3D Viewport — Sidebar — View — Lock Camera to View
commands.description: While in camera view, viewport navigation moves the camera itself, letting you frame a shot with the usual orbit and pan controls. Remember to untick it afterwards or you will nudge your composition by accident.

commands.name: Loop Cut and Slide
commands.menu: 3D Viewport — Edit Mode — Toolbar — Loop Cut
commands.description: Inserts a new edge loop running around the mesh; scroll for multiple evenly spaced loops, then slide to position (or right-click to leave them centred). The main way to add subdivision exactly where you need it — floor lines on a tower, or control loops before subdivision surfaces.

commands.name: Make Links
commands.description: Connects the outputs of selected nodes to the inputs of the active one. Quicker than dragging noodles once a graph gets dense.

commands.name: Make Node Group
commands.description: Collapses the selected nodes into a reusable group with its own inputs and outputs. Build a brick or concrete material group once and reuse it across every project.

commands.name: Make Segment
commands.menu: 3D Viewport — Edit Mode (Curve) — Curve — Make Segment
commands.description: Connects two selected end points with a new segment, joining separate splines within the same curve object. The curve equivalent of making an edge between vertices.

commands.name: Make Single User
commands.menu: 3D Viewport — Object Mode — Object — Relations — Make Single User
commands.description: Breaks shared data links so a linked duplicate gets its own independent copy of the mesh or material. Use it when one instance of a repeated element needs to become unique.

commands.name: Mark Seam
commands.menu: 3D Viewport — Edit Mode — Edge — Mark Seam
commands.description: Flags the selected edges as UV seams — the lines along which the surface will be cut open when unwrapping. Place seams where a real material would naturally break: internal corners, junctions and hidden edges.

commands.name: Mark Sharp
commands.menu: 3D Viewport — Edit Mode — Edge — Mark Sharp
commands.description: Tags edges as sharp so smooth shading breaks across them. Combine with Shade Smooth by Angle to keep crisp arrises on otherwise smoothed forms.

commands.name: Material Slots
commands.description: The list of materials an object carries; each face is assigned to one slot. Multiple slots let a single wall object carry plaster inside, brick outside and a painted reveal.

commands.name: Measure Tool
commands.description: Drags dimension lines between points in the viewport, snapping to geometry when Ctrl is held, and can also read angles off surfaces. The quickest sanity check that a stair, corridor or ceiling height is actually the size you intended.

commands.name: Menu Search
commands.description: Type-to-search across every menu entry available in the current context and run it directly. The fastest way to find a command whose shortcut you have forgotten.

commands.name: Merge
commands.description: Collapses the selected vertices into one, at the centre, the cursor, the first or last selected, or by collapsing each edge. Essential for closing gaps and tidying topology after joins.

commands.name: Merge by Distance
commands.menu: 3D Viewport — Edit Mode — Mesh — Merge — By Distance
commands.description: Welds together all selected vertices closer than a threshold distance. The standard cleanup for imported CAD geometry full of coincident duplicate vertices — run it and watch the vertex count drop.

commands.name: Mirror Modifier
commands.description: Mirrors the mesh live across the object's origin or another object such as an empty, with optional clipping so geometry cannot cross the mirror plane. Model half a symmetrical building and let the modifier maintain the other half.

commands.name: Mode Pie Menu
commands.description: Radial menu for switching between Object, Edit, Sculpt and the other interaction modes of the active object. Quicker than the header dropdown once it becomes muscle memory.

commands.name: Move
commands.description: Grabs the selection so it follows the mouse; click to confirm or right-click to cancel. Follow with X, Y or Z to lock the move to an axis, or type a number for an exact distance.

commands.name: Move to Collection
commands.menu: 3D Viewport — Object Mode — Object — Collection — Move to Collection
commands.description: Files the selected objects into an existing or new collection. Collections are Blender's layer system — organise a project into Structure, Envelope, Context, Furniture and so on, and toggle them in the Outliner.

commands.name: Multiresolution Modifier
commands.description: Stores multiple subdivision levels on one mesh so you can sculpt fine detail at high resolution while keeping a light base mesh. The sculpting-oriented sibling of Subdivision Surface.

commands.name: Mute Node
commands.menu: Shader Editor — Node — Toggle Node Mute
commands.description: Temporarily bypasses the selected nodes, passing data straight through. Perfect for A/B testing what a node — say, a roughness map — is contributing to the material.

commands.name: New Edge/Face from Vertices
commands.menu: 3D Viewport — Edit Mode — Vertex — New Edge/Face from Vertices
commands.description: Creates an edge between two selected vertices or a face across three or more. The bread-and-butter tool for manually stitching geometry together and closing openings.

commands.name: New Material
commands.description: Creates a material on the active object, based on the Principled BSDF shader. Name materials by finish — Concrete Fair-Faced, Oak Flooring, Glass Clear — and reuse them across objects for a consistent palette.

commands.name: Next Frame
commands.description: Steps the playhead forward one frame. Frame-by-frame stepping is how you catch a camera clipping through a doorway.

commands.name: NLA Push Down
commands.menu: Nonlinear Animation — Edit — Push Down Action
commands.description: Converts the object's current action into a strip in the Nonlinear Animation editor, where clips can be layered, repeated and blended. Useful for assembling long presentations from reusable camera moves.

commands.name: Numeric Transform Input
commands.description: Typing numbers during any transform applies exact values — G, X, 2.4, Enter moves precisely 2.4 units along X. With scene units set to metric this is how you model to real dimensions.

commands.name: Offset Edge Slide
commands.menu: 3D Viewport — Edit Mode — Edge — Offset Edge Slide
commands.description: Adds a new edge loop either side of the selected one and slides them symmetrically. Handy for framing a feature line with evenly spaced parallel loops in one action.

commands.name: Open
commands.description: Opens an existing .blend file. The Recent list under File is usually quicker for project files you touch daily.

commands.name: Opposite View
commands.description: Holding Ctrl with the numpad view keys flips to the opposite side: back, left or bottom. Handy for checking the rear elevation or underside without orbiting manually.

commands.name: Orbit View
commands.description: Rotates the viewport around the current view centre so you can inspect a model from any angle. The workhorse of viewport navigation — combine it with Frame Selected to keep orbiting around the object you care about.

commands.name: Outliner Visibility Toggle
commands.description: The eye, camera and screen icons beside each object and collection in the Outliner control viewport visibility, render visibility and selectability. Turning off render visibility for context massing keeps it out of final images while still on screen.

commands.name: Output Resolution and Format
commands.description: Sets render resolution, aspect, frame range and file format/path. For print deliverables work out pixel size from the target physical size and DPI; PNG for stills, and image sequences rather than video files for long animations.

commands.name: Pack Islands
commands.description: Rearranges all UV islands to fit efficiently within the 0–1 texture square with even spacing. Run it after unwrapping so no texture space is wasted.

commands.name: Pan View
commands.description: Slides the view sideways or vertically without rotating it. Use it to re-centre a facade or plan while keeping your current viewing angle.

commands.name: Paste Objects
commands.menu: 3D Viewport — Object Mode — Object — Paste Objects
commands.description: Pastes objects copied with Ctrl+C, even from another Blender instance. A lightweight way to pull a detail or asset from one project file into another.

commands.name: Pin UVs
commands.description: Pins the selected UV vertices so subsequent unwraps leave them exactly where you placed them. Pin the corners you have aligned to a texture, then re-unwrap and the rest follows.

commands.name: Pivot Point Pie Menu
commands.description: Chooses what transforms pivot around: median point, 3D cursor, individual origins, active element or bounding box centre. Switching to 3D Cursor lets you rotate a stair flight about a newel post, or scale a facade from one corner.

commands.name: Plane Lock
commands.description: Holding Shift with an axis key during a transform excludes that axis, constraining movement to the remaining plane. Shift+Z, for instance, slides objects around the ground plane without changing their height.

commands.name: Play Animation
commands.description: Plays the animation from the current frame in every open editor. If playback stutters, the viewport cannot keep up with the scene — the final render will still be smooth.

commands.name: Play Animation in Reverse
commands.description: Plays backwards from the current frame. Occasionally useful for scrubbing back through a walkthrough to find a moment.

commands.name: Precision Mode
commands.description: Holding Shift during a transform slows the movement right down for fine adjustment. Combine with axis locking when nudging elements into final position.

commands.name: Preferences
commands.description: Opens Blender's preferences: keymap, themes, add-ons and input settings. This is where you enable extensions such as Node Wrangler or import add-ons, and where you can turn on Emulate Numpad for laptops.

commands.name: Preview Node Output
commands.description: With the bundled Node Wrangler add-on enabled, Ctrl+Shift+clicking any node temporarily wires it to the output so you see exactly what it produces. Indispensable for debugging texture chains — enable Node Wrangler in Preferences first.

commands.name: Previous Frame
commands.description: Steps the playhead back one frame. Pairs with Next Frame for fine inspection of movement.

commands.name: Principled BSDF
commands.menu: Shader Editor — Add — Shader — Principled BSDF
commands.description: The physically based uber-shader behind almost every material: base colour, roughness, metallic, transmission and more in one node. Most real-world finishes need only a handful of its sliders — glass is mainly transmission, brushed steel is metallic plus roughness.

commands.name: Principled Texture Setup
commands.description: With Node Wrangler enabled and a Principled BSDF selected, this imports a folder of PBR texture maps — colour, roughness, normal, displacement — and wires them all correctly in one step. Turns setting up a downloaded material library texture into a five-second job.

commands.name: Project from View
commands.menu: 3D Viewport — Edit Mode — UV — Project from View
commands.description: Maps UVs directly from the current viewport angle, like projecting a slide onto the model. Ideal for mapping a facade photograph onto a flat elevation surface.

commands.name: Proportional Editing
commands.description: Transforms fall off smoothly onto surrounding geometry within an adjustable radius (scroll to resize during the transform). Use it to shape terrain or gently deform a surface without harsh steps.

commands.name: Proportional Falloff
commands.description: Cycles the proportional editing falloff profile — smooth, sphere, sharp, linear, random and more. Different profiles give very different landforms when sculpting site topography from a grid.

commands.name: Quick Favourites
commands.description: A personal pop-up menu of commands you have bookmarked; right-click any menu item and choose Add to Quick Favourites to include it. Build one per workflow — for example your most-used modifiers.

commands.name: Recalculate Normals Inside
commands.menu: 3D Viewport — Edit Mode — Mesh — Normals — Recalculate Inside
commands.description: Points all selected normals inward — the inverse of Recalculate Outside. Occasionally needed for interior-only shells such as a room used as a set for interior renders.

commands.name: Recalculate Normals Outside
commands.menu: 3D Viewport — Edit Mode — Mesh — Normals — Recalculate Outside
commands.description: Makes all selected face normals point outward from the enclosed volume. Fixes the classic symptoms of flipped normals — black faces in renders, inside-out booleans and shading artefacts.

commands.name: Redo
commands.description: Re-applies a change you have just undone. Combined with Undo it lets you flick between two states to compare a design decision.

commands.name: Remesh Modifier
commands.description: Rebuilds the mesh with uniform topology, most usefully in voxel mode. Good for consolidating messy boolean results or scan data into a single watertight surface, at the cost of sharp detail.

commands.name: Rename Object
commands.description: Pops up a small field to rename the active object in place. Consistent naming pays off enormously once a scene grows past a few dozen objects.

commands.name: Render Animation
commands.description: Renders every frame in the scene's frame range to the output path. Set the output folder and format in Output Properties first — frames write to disk as they finish, so an interrupted render keeps its progress.

commands.name: Render Image
commands.description: Renders a still from the active camera with the current engine and settings. Remember to save the result from the render window — it is not written to disk automatically.

commands.name: Render Region
commands.menu: 3D Viewport — View — View Regions — Render Region
commands.description: Drag a box (in camera view) to restrict rendering to just that region of the frame. Ideal for test-rendering one tricky corner of an image without paying for the whole frame.

commands.name: Rendered Viewport Shading
commands.description: Displays the viewport using the actual render engine, complete with lights and world environment. Design lighting interactively here rather than guessing and pressing F12.

commands.name: Repeat Last
commands.description: Runs the previous operation again with the same settings — for example re-applying an identical move or subdivide. Useful for rhythmic, repetitive edits such as spacing mullions.

commands.name: Right View
commands.description: Aligns the viewport to look along the -X axis for a side elevation. Hold Ctrl to jump to the opposite (left) side instead.

commands.name: Rip Vertices
commands.menu: 3D Viewport — Edit Mode — Vertex — Rip Vertices
commands.description: Tears the mesh apart along the selected vertices or edges, creating a hole and letting you drag one side away. Useful for opening a surface along a line, such as splitting a roof plane at the ridge.

commands.name: Rip Vertices and Fill
commands.menu: 3D Viewport — Edit Mode — Vertex — Rip Vertices and Fill
commands.description: Like Rip, but fills the gap left behind with new faces as you pull the ripped edge away. Extends a surface from an existing edge without leaving a hole.

commands.name: Rotate
commands.description: Rotates the selection around the current pivot point and view axis. Add an axis key and a number — for example R, Z, 45 — for a precise plan rotation.

commands.name: Save
commands.description: Saves the current .blend file. Blender also writes numbered backups (.blend1) alongside, which can rescue you after a bad save.

commands.name: Save As
commands.description: Saves the file under a new name or location. Use the + button in the file browser to auto-increment a version number — a simple way to keep design iterations.

commands.name: Scale
commands.description: Scales the selection about the pivot point. Constrain with an axis key to stretch in one direction, or type a factor such as 2 or 0.5 for exact resizing.

commands.name: Scene Units
commands.description: Sets the unit system (metric or imperial), length unit and unit scale for the scene. Set this to metric metres or millimetres at the start of every architectural project so typed dimensions and the Measure tool speak your language.

commands.name: Screw Modifier
commands.description: Sweeps a profile around an axis, optionally advancing per revolution like a thread. The instant way to generate spiral stairs, turned balusters and other surfaces of revolution from a simple section.

commands.name: Sculpt Brush Size
commands.description: Press F, move the mouse to resize the brush, and click to confirm. Constantly varying brush size is the key to controlled sculpting — big for landform, small for detail.

commands.name: Sculpt Brush Strength
commands.description: Adjusts how strongly the brush deforms the surface, previewed interactively like brush size. Keep strength low and build form in passes for the most control.

commands.name: Select All
commands.description: Selects everything in the current mode. Double-tap A or use Alt+A to clear the selection instead.

commands.name: Select Less
commands.menu: 3D Viewport — Edit Mode — Select — Select More/Less — Less
commands.description: Shrinks the selection inward by one ring of elements. Pair with Select More to erode a selection's ragged border.

commands.name: Select Linked
commands.menu: 3D Viewport — Edit Mode — Select — Select Linked
commands.description: Hovering over geometry and pressing L selects everything physically connected to it; Ctrl+L expands the current selection to its connected mesh. The quickest way to grab one loose part inside an object containing many.

commands.name: Select Linked Objects
commands.description: Selects objects that share data with the active one — same object data, material, collection or parent. Quickly finds every instance of a repeated component across a scene.

commands.name: Select More
commands.menu: 3D Viewport — Edit Mode — Select — Select More/Less — More
commands.description: Grows the selection outward by one ring of neighbouring elements each press. Useful for expanding from a seed selection to a whole region.

commands.name: Select Similar
commands.menu: 3D Viewport — Edit Mode — Select — Select Similar
commands.description: Selects elements sharing a property with the current selection — same material, normal direction, face area, edge length and more. Selecting all coplanar faces by normal is a fast route to every face of one orientation on a facade.

commands.name: Separate
commands.description: Moves the selected geometry (or all loose parts, or each material) into a new object. The counterpart to Join — use it to break a monolithic import into workable pieces.

commands.name: Set 3D Cursor
commands.description: Places the 3D cursor in the scene, snapping to surfaces under the mouse. The cursor is Blender's universal reference point: new objects appear there and it can serve as pivot or origin target.

commands.name: Set Active Camera
commands.menu: 3D Viewport — View — Cameras — Set Active Object as Camera
commands.description: Makes the selected camera the one used for rendering and camera view. Essential in scenes with multiple saved viewpoints.

commands.name: Set Curve Radius
commands.menu: 3D Viewport — Edit Mode (Curve) — Control Points — Radius
commands.description: Scales the per-point radius that multiplies any bevel profile along the curve. Taper a swept tube — a branching column, a shaped handrail — by varying radius along its length.

commands.name: Set Frame Range
commands.description: Defines the start and end frames for playback and rendering. At the default 24 fps, a 10-second walkthrough is 240 frames — set the range before rendering an animation.

commands.name: Set Handle Type
commands.menu: 3D Viewport — Edit Mode (Curve) — Control Points — Set Handle Type
commands.description: Switches selected Bézier handles between Automatic, Aligned, Free and Vector. Vector handles give straight, polyline-like segments — the right choice for orthogonal building outlines — while Aligned keeps curves flowing smoothly.

commands.name: Set Keyframe Handle Type
commands.description: Changes the handle behaviour of selected keys — Auto Clamped for smooth default motion, Vector for sharp direction changes, Free for manual control. The same handle logic as Bézier curves, applied to time.

commands.name: Set Keyframe Interpolation
commands.description: Sets how values move between the selected keyframes — Constant, Linear or Bézier, plus eased variants. Linear suits a steady walkthrough pace; Bézier gives natural starts and stops.

commands.name: Set Origin to 3D Cursor
commands.menu: 3D Viewport — Object Mode — Object — Set Origin — Origin to 3D Cursor
commands.description: Places the object's origin exactly at the 3D cursor. Snap the cursor to a corner first and you get a precise pivot — for example the hinge edge of a door.

commands.name: Set Origin to Geometry
commands.menu: 3D Viewport — Object Mode — Object — Set Origin — Origin to Geometry
commands.description: Moves the object's origin point to the centre of its geometry without moving the mesh. Fixes objects that rotate or scale around a point far from where they sit.

commands.name: Set Parent
commands.description: Parents the selected objects to the active one so they move, rotate and scale with it. Use it to make furniture follow a room, or fittings follow a wall, while remaining independently editable.

commands.name: Shade Flat
commands.menu: 3D Viewport — Object Mode — Object — Shade Flat
commands.description: Shows each face with its own flat normal, giving crisp facets. The right look for hard-edged architectural elements and for diagnosing smoothing problems.

commands.name: Shade Smooth
commands.menu: 3D Viewport — Object Mode — Object — Shade Smooth
commands.description: Renders the surface with smooth shading, blending normals across faces so curved forms look continuous without extra geometry. Purely a display treatment — the mesh itself is unchanged.

commands.name: Shade Smooth by Angle
commands.menu: 3D Viewport — Object Mode — Object — Shade Smooth by Angle
commands.description: Smooths shading only across edges shallower than a chosen angle, keeping sharp creases crisp. In Blender 4.1+ this replaced the old Auto Smooth checkbox and is the go-to for mixed curved/hard surfaces such as columns with fillets.

commands.name: Shading Pie Menu
commands.description: Radial menu switching between Wireframe, Solid, Material Preview and Rendered viewport shading. Flick to Material Preview to judge finishes, or Rendered to check lighting without a full render.

commands.name: Show Hidden
commands.menu: 3D Viewport — Object — Show/Hide — Show Hidden Objects
commands.description: Reveals everything hidden with H or Shift+H. If objects seem to have vanished, try this before assuming they were deleted.

commands.name: Show/Hide Render Window
commands.description: Reopens the window showing the last render without re-rendering. Useful for comparing the latest result against viewport changes.

commands.name: Shrink/Fatten
commands.menu: 3D Viewport — Edit Mode — Mesh — Transform — Shrink/Fatten
commands.description: Moves selected geometry along its own normals, pushing a surface outward or pulling it inward. Think of it as inflating or deflating — useful for offsetting a roof surface or adjusting wall thickness locally.

commands.name: Shrinkwrap Modifier
commands.description: Projects or wraps the mesh onto the surface of a target object. Use it to drape a road or path mesh over terrain, or conform panelling to a doubly curved surface.

commands.name: Simple Deform Modifier
commands.menu: Properties — Modifier Properties — Deform — Simple Deform
commands.description: Applies a single parametric deformation — twist, bend, taper or stretch — around an axis. The quick route to a twisting tower study or a tapered mast.

commands.name: Skin Modifier
commands.description: Wraps a mesh skeleton of edges in solid geometry, with per-vertex radius control (Ctrl+A in Edit Mode resizes). Draw a space-frame or branching structure as edges and let Skin flesh out the members.

commands.name: Smart UV Project
commands.menu: 3D Viewport — Edit Mode — UV — Smart UV Project
commands.description: Automatically unwraps by slicing the mesh into projections based on face angles — no seams required. Not as tidy as manual seams, but perfectly serviceable for quickly texturing massing models and context buildings.

commands.name: Smooth (Hold Shift)
commands.description: Holding Shift with any sculpt brush temporarily switches to smoothing, relaxing bumps and noise. The universal cleanup gesture between shaping strokes.

commands.name: Smooth Vertices
commands.menu: 3D Viewport — Edit Mode — Vertex — Smooth Vertices
commands.description: Relaxes the selected vertices by averaging them with their neighbours, ironing out lumps and kinks. Run it a few times on messy terrain or scan data to calm the surface.

commands.name: Snap Cursor to Selected
commands.menu: 3D Viewport — Object — Snap — Cursor to Selected
commands.description: Moves the 3D cursor to the selection — a single vertex, an edge midpoint or the median of several elements. Step one of many precision moves: mark the reference point, then snap or pivot to it.

commands.name: Snap Cursor to World Origin
commands.menu: 3D Viewport — Object — Snap — Cursor to World Origin
commands.description: Returns the 3D cursor to 0,0,0. Do this before adding objects that should start at the project origin, or after cursor-based operations leave it somewhere odd.

commands.name: Snap Pie Menu
commands.description: A pie of snap actions moving the selection or the 3D cursor to one another, to the grid or to the world origin. The backbone of precise placement workflows in Blender.

commands.name: Snap Selection to Cursor
commands.menu: 3D Viewport — Object — Snap — Selection to Cursor
commands.description: Teleports the selected objects or elements to the 3D cursor's position. Snap the cursor to a corner first and you can land an object exactly on that corner.

commands.name: Snapping Settings
commands.description: Opens the snapping options: what to snap to (increment, grid, vertex, edge, face centre), what part of the selection snaps, and extras such as snapping rotation to face normals. Worth setting up deliberately — good snap settings are the difference between CAD-like precision and guesswork.

commands.name: Solidify Modifier
commands.description: Gives thickness to single-sided surfaces, turning a plane into a wall or a shell into a slab, with control over offset direction and rim faces. Model buildings as thin surfaces and let Solidify carry the construction thickness — changing a wall build-up becomes a single number.

commands.name: Split
commands.menu: 3D Viewport — Edit Mode — Mesh — Split — Selection
commands.description: Disconnects the selected geometry from the rest of the mesh without moving it or making a new object. Use it when part of a surface must become independent — for example detaching a door leaf from its wall while staying in the same object.

commands.name: Subdivide
commands.menu: 3D Viewport — Edit Mode — Context Menu — Subdivide
commands.description: Splits the selected edges and faces into smaller ones, with a cut count in the operator panel. Use it to add resolution to a plane before proportional-editing it into terrain, or to refine a region for detail.

commands.name: Subdivide Curve
commands.description: Adds control points between the selected ones, increasing local control over the curve's shape. Subdivide sparingly — fewer points generally means fairer curves.

commands.name: Subdivision Surface Modifier
commands.menu: Properties — Modifier Properties — Generate — Subdivision Surface
commands.description: Smooths the mesh by subdividing it, using the cage as a control net; Ctrl+1 to Ctrl+5 adds the modifier at that viewport level directly. Use it with Edge Crease or support loops for furniture, sanitaryware and other curved elements.

commands.name: Sun Position
commands.description: An add-on (bundled historically, via Extensions in 4.2+) that places a Sun light astronomically from latitude, longitude, date and time. Essential for honest daylight and shadow studies — set the site coordinates and step through solstice and equinox conditions.

commands.name: Symmetrize
commands.description: Mirrors one half of the mesh onto the other across a chosen axis, overwriting the target side. Use it to restore perfect symmetry to a model that has drifted during editing.

commands.name: Timeline
commands.description: The strip along the bottom of the default workspace showing the playhead, frame range and keyframes of the selected object. Scrub by dragging in it; most playback controls live in its header.

commands.name: To Sphere
commands.menu: 3D Viewport — Edit Mode — Mesh — Transform — To Sphere
commands.description: Pushes the selected vertices toward a perfect spherical arrangement by an adjustable factor. Useful for rounding a boxy form into a dome or correcting a distorted circular opening.

commands.name: Toggle Camera View
commands.description: Jumps into the active camera so you see exactly what will render. Press again to drop back to the free viewport.

commands.name: Toggle Cyclic
commands.menu: 3D Viewport — Edit Mode (Curve) — Curve — Toggle Cyclic
commands.description: Closes the curve into a loop or opens it again. Closed curves can be filled and extruded into solids, which makes them a tidy way to model floor plates from a drawn outline.

commands.name: Toggle Edit Mode
commands.description: Switches the active object between Object Mode and Edit Mode, where you work on its vertices, edges and faces. The single most-used mode switch in Blender.

commands.name: Toggle Local View
commands.description: Isolates the selected objects in a temporary view, hiding everything else. Ideal for working on one component of a busy building model; press again to return to the full scene.

commands.name: Toggle Maximise Area
commands.description: Expands the editor under the mouse to fill the whole window, and back again. Great for temporarily giving the 3D Viewport or Shader Editor your full screen.

commands.name: Toggle Perspective/Orthographic
commands.description: Switches the viewport between perspective and orthographic projection. Orthographic removes foreshortening, which is what you want for elevation-style views and precise modelling; perspective is better for judging how a space will actually read.

commands.name: Toggle Sculpt Mode
commands.description: Enters Sculpt Mode, where brushes push, pull and smooth the mesh like clay. For architects it is most useful on terrain, landform studies and organic shell forms.

commands.name: Toggle Sidebar
commands.description: Shows or hides the sidebar with the Item, Tool and View tabs, including exact transform values and dimensions. This is where you type precise sizes for elements rather than eyeballing them.

commands.name: Toggle Snapping
commands.description: Turns persistent snapping on or off, using whatever snap target is set in the header (increment, vertex, edge, face and so on). Vertex snapping is the everyday tool for making walls, slabs and fittings meet exactly.

commands.name: Toggle Toolbar
commands.description: Shows or hides the left-hand toolbar of active tools such as Move, Measure and Annotate. Hide it to reclaim viewport space once you know the shortcuts.

commands.name: Toggle Wireframe
commands.description: Flips the viewport between solid and wireframe display. Wireframe reads like a line drawing and makes it easy to see through massing studies or select hidden geometry.

commands.name: Toggle X-Ray
commands.description: Makes geometry semi-transparent so you can see and select through surfaces. Crucial in Edit Mode: with X-Ray on, box selection grabs the vertices on the far side of the mesh as well as the near side.

commands.name: Top View
commands.description: Looks straight down the Z axis, giving a plan view of the scene. Essential when blocking out site layouts or checking alignments from above.

commands.name: Trackball Rotate
commands.description: Pressing R twice switches to free trackball rotation, tumbling the selection in any direction rather than around a single axis. Useful for casually orienting props and scatter objects.

commands.name: Transform Orientation Pie Menu
commands.description: Switches the axes transforms align to: global, local, normal, view or a custom orientation. Set a custom orientation from an angled wall to move things square to that wall rather than to the world.

commands.name: Triangulate Faces
commands.menu: 3D Viewport — Edit Mode — Face — Triangulate Faces
commands.description: Converts the selected faces into triangles. Some game engines and analysis tools want triangulated meshes; run this deliberately at export time rather than modelling in triangles.

commands.name: Triangulate Modifier
commands.description: Triangulates the mesh non-destructively, typically as the last modifier before export to engines that require triangles. Keeps your working file in clean quads while the output is triangulated.

commands.name: Tris to Quads
commands.menu: 3D Viewport — Edit Mode — Face — Tris to Quads
commands.description: Merges pairs of triangles back into quads where they form sensible rectangles. Together with Limited Dissolve it is the standard treatment for triangulated imports from CAD or BIM tools.

commands.name: Un-Subdivide
commands.description: Removes alternating edge loops to reduce mesh density while preserving overall shape where the grid is regular. A quick densitiy reducer for over-subdivided imported surfaces.

commands.name: Undo
commands.description: Steps back through recent changes. Blender keeps separate undo behaviour per mode, so if a change seems stuck, check you are in the mode where you made it.

commands.name: Ungroup Nodes
commands.description: Dissolves a node group back into its constituent nodes in the current tree. Use it when a shared group needs a one-off local variation.

commands.name: Unpin UVs
commands.description: Releases pinned UV vertices so unwrapping can move them again. The counterpart to Pin when iterating on a layout.

commands.name: Unwrap
commands.description: Flattens the selected mesh into 2D UV coordinates, cutting along marked seams, so image textures can be applied without stretching. Good seams first, then unwrap — the order matters.

commands.name: UV Sync Selection
commands.menu: UV Editor — Header — UV Sync Selection
commands.description: Links selection between the 3D Viewport and the UV Editor so picking faces in one highlights them in the other. Turn it on when hunting for which wall a distorted island belongs to.

commands.name: Vertex Bevel
commands.menu: 3D Viewport — Edit Mode — Vertex — Bevel Vertices
commands.description: Bevels selected vertices rather than edges, cutting each corner back into a flat or rounded chamfer. Useful for splayed corners on plans and easing sharp junctions in profiles.

commands.name: Vertex Select Mode
commands.description: Switches Edit Mode selection to vertices. Hold Shift while pressing 1, 2 or 3 to enable several select modes at once.

commands.name: Vertex Slide
commands.menu: 3D Viewport — Edit Mode — Vertex — Slide Vertices
commands.description: Slides a vertex along one of its connected edges. Perfect for nudging a point along a wall line without drifting off the surface.

commands.name: View Layers
commands.description: Renders subsets of collections as separate layers, with per-layer passes for compositing. Use them to output a building and its context separately, or to produce clay and textured versions of one view.

commands.name: View Pie Menu
commands.description: A radial menu of viewpoint options — front, top, camera, frame selected and more — under a single key. Useful on laptops without a numpad.

commands.name: Voxel Remesh
commands.description: Rebuilds the sculpt as an even voxel-based mesh at the current voxel size, fusing overlapping parts into one watertight surface. Remesh regularly while sculpting to keep geometry uniform and workable.

commands.name: Walk Navigation
commands.description: First-person navigation using WASD and the mouse, with optional gravity. The closest thing to walking a client through a building inside the viewport — invaluable for checking spatial proportions at eye level.

commands.name: Weld Modifier
commands.description: Merges vertices within a threshold distance, non-destructively. Useful at the end of a Mirror or Array stack to fuse coincident seams without editing the mesh.

commands.name: Wireframe Modifier
commands.description: Replaces the mesh with solid members along its edges, like a physical wireframe model. Turn a gridded surface into a gridshell or space-frame study in seconds.

commands.name: World Environment (HDRI)
commands.description: Sets the scene's ambient environment; plugging an HDRI image into the World's Environment Texture gives realistic sky light and reflections in one move. The single biggest lighting upgrade for most architectural renders.

commands.name: Zoom Region
commands.description: Drag a box and the view zooms to fill it with that region. Faster than scroll-zooming when you need to dive into a specific junction or detail.

commands.name: Zoom View
commands.description: Moves the view closer to or further from the point of interest. Dragging with Ctrl+MMB gives smooth zooming, which is easier to control than the stepped scroll wheel when working on detail.
